title: Host warden: the one process per machine that acts on the memory of processes that already run (suspend, resume, cancel), from the same host sample and the same ladder the admission gates read.

Policy.description: The authored numbers of the ladder and of the loop. Shares are basis points of the physical memory, bounded by a minimum and a maximum in megabytes, so a 4 GB host and a 128 GB host both get a usable line. Headroom is the memory the host can still give out before the OS halts applications: the available memory plus the swap room, and the swap room is the free swap plus the swap that can still grow, which is the free space of the swap volume minus swapDiskReserveMegabytes (never below 0; 0 where the swap volume is unknown or cannot grow), the sum bounded by swapRoomMaximumBasisPoints of the physical memory; a host that reports no swap has no headroom and keeps the available-memory law. Headroom below the headroomGuard line is guard, below the headroomDanger line is danger. defaultMode is the mode of a machine without a valid mode file: observe decides and alarms without signalling, enforce acts; the whole fleet is switched by changing this one value, every warden restarts itself on the changed source digest. ensureMilliseconds is the time a process trusts its own earlier ensure before it looks at the warden again. heavySuspendMaximumSeconds is the longer suspend maximum of a declared final link (a compile unit of the final kind on the carving list of the admission policy): such a unit is also the dearest to lose among the compile units, so it is suspended last and kept running first; the danger-line cancel is unchanged. requeueMaximumAttempts, requeuePollMilliseconds and requeueCalmMaximumSeconds bound the automatic requeue of a build whose process the warden cancelled for memory: it waits for a calm host (polling the state) at most requeueCalmMaximumSeconds, is admitted again through capacity admission, and ends with the typed failure after requeueMaximumAttempts attempts. Swap traffic (pages swapped out plus swapped in per second) was measured on a 16 GB macOS host (240 one-second samples while builds ran, the kernel at normal, 2.7 to 6.1 GB available) at a median of 0, a 90th percentile of 2.9, a 99th percentile of 10.9 and a single 285 MB/s burst, so swapActiveMegabytesPerSecond (64) lies far above healthy paging and swapSustainedSeconds (10) ignores a burst; swapping counts as worked only when it is sustained, and it is acute (severe, cancels) only together with the OS pressure at least warn and the available memory below the resume line. The compressed memory is reclaimable: the same host held 3.2 to 7.9 GB compressed (20 to 48 percent, above 35 percent in 60 percent of the samples) while healthy, so compressedGuardBasisPoints (55 percent) and compressedDangerBasisPoints (70 percent) lie above it and compressed memory never decides a cancel alone.
Policy.descriptionDe: Die festgelegten Zahlen der Leiter und der Schleife. Die Reserve (headroom) ist der Speicher, den der Host noch vergeben kann, bevor das Betriebssystem Anwendungen anhaelt: der verfuegbare Speicher plus der Swap-Spielraum; der Spielraum ist der freie Swap plus der noch wachsende Swap, also der freie Platz des Swap-Volumes abzueglich swapDiskReserveMegabytes (nie unter 0; 0 wo das Swap-Volume unbekannt ist oder nicht wachsen kann), die Summe begrenzt auf swapRoomMaximumBasisPoints des physischen Speichers; ein Host ohne Swap hat keine Reserve und behaelt das Gesetz des verfuegbaren Speichers. Reserve unter der Linie headroomGuard ist guard, unter der Linie headroomDanger ist danger. defaultMode ist der Modus einer Maschine ohne gueltige mode-Datei: observe entscheidet und alarmiert ohne Signale, enforce handelt; die ganze Flotte wird durch diesen einen Wert umgeschaltet, jeder Waechter startet sich beim geaenderten Quelltext-Digest selbst neu. ensureMilliseconds ist die Zeit, in der ein Prozess seinem eigenen frueheren Ensure vertraut, bevor er wieder nach dem Waechter sieht. heavySuspendMaximumSeconds ist das längere Anhaltemaximum eines deklarierten Final-Links (eine Kompilationseinheit der Art final auf der Carving-Liste der Admission-Richtlinie): eine solche Einheit ist unter den Kompilationseinheiten auch die teuerste zu verlieren, wird also zuletzt angehalten und zuerst weiterlaufen gelassen; der Abbruch an der Gefahrenlinie bleibt unverändert. requeueMaximumAttempts, requeuePollMilliseconds und requeueCalmMaximumSeconds begrenzen das automatische erneute Einreihen eines Builds, dessen Prozess der Wächter wegen Speicher abgebrochen hat: er wartet höchstens requeueCalmMaximumSeconds auf einen ruhigen Host (Abfrage des Zustands), wird über die Kapazitätszulassung erneut zugelassen und endet nach requeueMaximumAttempts Versuchen mit dem typisierten Fehler. Der Swap-Verkehr (ausgelagerte plus eingelagerte Seiten je Sekunde) wurde auf einem 16-GB-macOS-Host gemessen (240 Ein-Sekunden-Proben während Builds liefen, Kernel normal, 2,7 bis 6,1 GB verfügbar) mit Median 0, 90. Perzentil 2,9, 99. Perzentil 10,9 und einem einzigen Stoß von 285 MB/s; swapActiveMegabytesPerSecond (64) liegt weit darüber und swapSustainedSeconds (10) überhört einen Stoß. Swapping zählt nur, wenn es anhält, und ist nur zusammen mit mindestens Druckwarnung und verfügbarem Speicher unter der Wiederaufnahmelinie akut (schwer, bricht ab). Der komprimierte Speicher ist rückgewinnbar: derselbe Host hielt gesund 3,2 bis 7,9 GB komprimiert (20 bis 48 Prozent, in 60 Prozent der Proben über 35 Prozent), die Linien compressedGuardBasisPoints (55 Prozent) und compressedDangerBasisPoints (70 Prozent) liegen darüber, und komprimierter Speicher entscheidet nie allein über einen Abbruch.

Kinds.description: Ordered kinds of subjects: the first entry whose pattern matches the command line of a process that is a subject candidate (below a root, or matching an identity) names its kind. A pattern may name the anchors <workspace> and <browsers> (see Anchors); a kind whose anchor is empty does not match. rank is the cost to redo (ascending = cheapest first), actions are what the warden may do, signal is what a cancel sends, scope is what a signal reaches (process: the pid, group: its process group, tree: the pid and every descendant, parent first). source is the repository path of the code that starts the process; a test proves every pattern names a path that exists there. A kind with `ceiling: "unit"` runs compile units: the runtime ceiling of its subject is derived from its command line by the admission law of the compile-memory policy (`Policy.unitCeiling` of the admission schema: the budget of the unit kind, or the declared `budgetMegabytes` of its carving entry) and is enforced at every level, see Ceiling.

Roots.description: Patterns over the command line that mark a process as repo-started: the workspace's pinned Bun runtime, the user-level pinned Bun runtime and the native build scheduler. A subject has a root among itself and its ancestors.

Anchors.description: Where this machine keeps what the repository starts. workspace is a pattern over a command line whose first group is the root of a workspace: every process that runs from the pinned cache of a workspace (its Bun runtime or its toolchains) names that workspace, so no root is hardcoded. browsers lists the directories of the repository browser runtime below a workspace; a test proves the entry equals what the repository computes with ensureRepositoryBrowserPathV1. The names <workspace> and <browsers> in Identities and Kinds stand for the alternation of every workspace root and of every browser directory found; a pattern whose anchor is empty is inactive.

Identities.description: Patterns over the command line of processes that are subject candidates by what they are, whatever their ancestry (an agent shell, a ticket script, a terminal): the pinned toolchain binaries of a workspace (cargo, rustc, rustdoc, clippy-driver), the cargo test and bench executables of a workspace (a deps directory of any target directory below it, the executable named with the 16 hex digits of its metadata hash), every process of the repository browser runtime, and cargo or a compile tool of any toolchain (a script that exports a user rustc to bypass the repository launcher included) whose command line names a path below a workspace (source, output, dependency or manifest). Never patterns, protected paths and the kinds still apply; a toolchain or a browser of the user (cargo home, Homebrew, rustup, the user-level Playwright cache, applications) matches none of them.

Swap.description: How the host warden reads the swap of the machine, every intervalMilliseconds (the numbers change slowly and each read spawns a command): macOS prints the swap file occupancy with usage (total, used, free) and the free space of the swap volume with disk (the first volume that answers; the swap files live on the data volume and cannot grow when it is full), Linux reads SwapTotal and SwapFree from meminfo (a swap partition or file does not grow; a host without swap reports null), Windows reports null (observe only). The free swap and the free swap volume are reported in whole megabytes, null where unknown.

Never.description: Patterns over the command line of processes that are never subjects, whatever they hold: the warden itself, the sidecar launcher and every sidecar role (cache server, agent, scheduler, graph, pool puller, Ready supervisor; the Ready stage wrapper below them is the one exception), the remote-execution entry, server and scheduler, the replica daemon and the fleet boot entry.

Platforms.description: Where signals are sent. Windows has no SIGSTOP and no ps: the warden decides and alarms there, it never signals (observe only).

Table.description: The command that reads the process table on unix, with the locale each platform needs to print non-ASCII command lines (ps escapes them otherwise). The full form prints every column; the loop reads the cheap columns every tick (pid, parent, group, resident, state, elapsed, CPU time, start) and the expensive command line only of processes it has not seen yet (key: pid and start text), one `-p` list, or the whole table from commandAllMinimum new processes on (a process younger than commandSettledSeconds, or one still printed as `(name)`, may not have executed its program yet, so its command line is read again on the next tick instead of kept): the command line column costs about three times the rest of the table together. `chargeMinimumKilobytes` is the resident size from which Linux reads `smaps_rollup` for a process (the table prints the resident set; macOS reads every process natively).

Other.description: One consumer the warden does not own: the topmost process of a tree outside every subject, with the resident megabytes of the whole tree. Reported, never touched.

swapFileMegabytes.description: The size of the largest swap file the kernel creates (macOS `vm.compressor.swapper.swapfile_size_max`): the swap that is still free is only safe while it holds more than one such file, because a burst of page-outs can outrun the creation of the next one. Absent: `swapFileDefaultMegabytes`.

intervalMilliseconds.description: The time since the previous sample, over which the swap traffic rate is averaged; it feeds the sustained swap timer. Absent: one tight tick.

ProcessRow.description: One process of the table. `memoryKilobytes` is what the kernel charges the process (macOS phys_footprint through proc_pid_rusage, Linux proportional plus swapped proportional set size of the processes that are resident enough to matter, Windows the private usage; `cpuSeconds`, present when the table has the CPU time column, is the CPU time the process has used so far), never the resident set that `ps` prints: macOS counts the pages an allocator freed but kept mapped (MADV_FREE_REUSABLE) as resident, which read a 3 GB browser tree as 5 GB. A process the kernel does not let us read keeps the resident set `ps` printed.

nonresidentKilobytes.description: Estimated process charge outside the resident set. Linux uses SwapPss. macOS uses positive physical footprint minus RSS.

nonresidentMegabytes.description: Estimated nonresident memory for all stopped processes in this subject's signal scope. Null means that one or more stopped processes could not be measured.

stoppedFootprintMegabytes.description: Total charge from the process table for stopped members of this signal scope when the nonresident portion is unknown.

lastResort.description: The subject owns a whole build tree: the danger cancel takes it after every other candidate.

keepsProgress.description: The subject is a foreground run of its owner that holds progress (a granted process tree): the warden may suspend and resume it, never cancel it, whatever the reason.

suspensions.description: How often the loop suspended this subject within flapWindowSeconds (set by the loop, not by classification).

resumedSeconds.description: Seconds since the loop resumed this subject, within flapWindowSeconds.

grantMegabytes.description: The memory the owner of this subject holds for it at the capacity gate (its claim, see Claim): a subject within it is sheltered, cancelled only when the host is in severe danger and after every subject above its grant.

held.description: True while the owner itself stopped the subject (its claim says stopped): the warden does not count it as suspended, never finds it overdue and never resumes it.

Ceiling.description: The runtime ceiling of a compile unit (the typed over-ceiling verdict is a subject whose megabytes exceed `megabytes`): `unit` is `<crate>|<target>` (target `host` without `--target`), `kind` the budget kind (`final` for a `cdylib` link unit, else `library`), `megabytes` the most its resident footprint may reach, `listed` whether the unit is on the closed carving list of the admission policy, then `measuredMegabytes` is its measured peak. An unlisted unit above it must be carved; a listed unit above it outgrew its declared budget. Both are cancelled at once, at every level of the ladder.

swapMilliseconds.description: The leaky swap timer the previous tick left (absent: 0).

resumedSeconds.description: Seconds since the warden last resumed a subject (absent: none yet); a recovered host resumes the next one only after resumeSettleSeconds.

swapMilliseconds.description: The leaky swap timer after this tick: it gains the sample interval while the swap traffic is at or above swapActiveMegabytesPerSecond and loses it otherwise, between 0 and twice swapSustainedSeconds; the swap counts as worked once it reaches swapSustainedSeconds.

Cancel.description: The record written before a cancel signal, so the owner of the process can tell a warden cancel from a crash and requeue instead of failing.

buildScriptOutput.description: Artifact directory of the cancelled build script, with the package, target and profile encoded by Cargo.

ancestors.description: The pids of the processes above the cancelled one, nearest first: the owner of a build finds the cancels that hit its own process tree by its pid, whatever the command line says.

Claim.description: What the owner of a process writes to claims/<pid>.json: the memory it holds for it at the capacity gate (grantMegabytes, a sheltered process is cancelled last) and whether the owner itself stopped it while it waits for more (stopped: the warden neither suspends, resumes nor finds it overdue). A claim older than claimMaximumMilliseconds is ignored.

Absent.description: The mirror record of a machine whose warden writes no fresh state: tells the coordinator no warden from no record.

Mirror.description: What a worker mirrors to the group store as memory.json: the state of its warden as written, or the absent record.

TreeRow.description: One process of the repository tree: the heaviest by CPU time, then memory.

foreign.description: What every process outside the subjects holds (footprint where readable, resident set otherwise): admission counts it against the floor. `heavy` is the number of such processes at or above `foreignHeavyMegabytes`; the warden does not end while one runs.

grants.description: The live grants of the capacity gate the warden saw and the megabytes they reserve; the warden does not end while one is live.

en.alarm: [warden] {action} {kind} pid {pid} ({owner}, {megabytes} MB): {reason}; host {available} MB available (guard {guard} MB, danger {danger} MB), swap {swap}, pressure {pressure}{headroom}{observed}

guard.available: available memory is below the guard line
guard.headroom: available memory plus swap that can still grow is below the headroom guard line
guard.critical: memory pressure is critical and available memory is below the resume line
guard.swap: swap-out rate is high and available memory is below the resume line
guard.swap-used: swap in use is above its line and available memory is below the resume line
guard.swap-share: the share of the swap in use is above its line and available memory is below the resume line
guard.compressed: compressed memory is above its line
guard.cap: a build-critical process crossed its memory cap
guard.swap-free: the swap that is still free is below one swap file, so a burst of page-outs can outrun the next swap file
guard.grant: a process runs well above the memory its grant reserved while the host has no spare memory

danger.available: available memory is below the danger line
danger.headroom: available memory plus swap that can still grow is below the headroom danger line
danger.swap-used: swap in use is above its danger line and available memory is below the guard line
danger.swap-share: the share of the swap in use is above its danger line and available memory is below the guard line
danger.compressed: compressed memory is above its danger line
danger.swap-free: the swap that is still free is below half a swap file, so the kernel can run out of swap before the next file exists
danger.swapping: the host is swapping memory out at a high rate while memory pressure is not critical yet

reasons.limit: it stayed suspended beyond the hard maximum without the host recovering; it is cancelled so its client can retry
reasons.cap: its memory is over the cap of {cap} MB for {kind}
reasons.capCrossed: its memory crossed the cap of {cap} MB for {kind}; it is a build-critical kind, so other work is held first and it is only killed when the host is critical
reasons.ceiling: unit {unit} peaked at {peak} MB, above its {ceilingKind} ceiling of {ceiling} MB, and it is not on the carving list: carve it along the domain taxonomy so that it fits
reasons.ceilingListed: unit {unit} peaked at {peak} MB, above its declared carving budget of {ceiling} MB (measured {measured} MB): carve it further, or measure it again and declare the new budget
reasons.guard: the host was short of memory (tight) and the process stayed suspended for too long
reasons.danger: the host was critically short of memory

grant.within: ; it held {megabytes} MB, within its grant of {grant} MB, and was taken only because the host was in danger
grant.over: ; it held {megabytes} MB, {excess} MB above its grant of {grant} MB

failure.head: [warden] the build cannot finish: the host warden cancelled {count} of its processes to keep this machine from running out of memory
failure.tail: Nothing is retried. Remove the cause named above (carve a unit that is over its ceiling) or wait until the host memory is calm, then run the command again.
failure.exhausted: It was queued again {retries} time(s) and the host memory did not stay calm. Wait until the host memory is calm, then run the command again.

requeue.wait: [warden] the host warden cancelled {count} of the processes of this build to keep the host from running out of memory ({kinds}); the build is queued again for capacity admission once the host memory is calm (attempt {attempt} of {maximum})
requeue.waiting: [warden] waiting for the host memory to be calm, {seconds} s of {limit} s, before the build is admitted again
requeue.admit: [warden] the build is admitted again (attempt {attempt} of {maximum})

en.held: [warden] {operation} waits: host memory is {level} ({trigger}); nothing heavy starts until it is calm (available {available} MB, swap in use {swap} MB, compressed {compressed} MB)
en.status: Memory guard: {level} ({mode}), {trigger}; available {available} of {total} MB, swap in use {swap} MB, compressed {compressed} MB, pressure {pressure}; suspended {suspended}, resumed {resumed}, cancelled {cancelled}
en.statusOthers: Memory guard: largest consumers it does not own: {others}
en.statusAbsent: Memory guard: no warden is running on this machine
en.locked: [warden] another warden holds the lock (pid {pid}); this one ends
en.left: [warden] resumed {kind} pid {pid}, left suspended by a predecessor
en.observeOnly: [warden] platform {platform} cannot suspend processes: observe mode only

de.alarm: [Wächter] {action} {kind} pid {pid} ({owner}, {megabytes} MB): {reason}; Host {available} MB verfügbar (Wache {guard} MB, Gefahr {danger} MB), Swap {swap}, Druck {pressure}{headroom}{observed}

guard.available: der verfügbare Speicher liegt unter der Wachlinie
guard.headroom: der verfügbare Speicher plus noch wachsender Swap liegt unter der Wachlinie der Reserve
guard.critical: der Speicherdruck ist kritisch und der verfügbare Speicher liegt unter der Wiederaufnahmelinie
guard.swap: die Swap-Auslagerungsrate ist hoch und der verfügbare Speicher liegt unter der Wiederaufnahmelinie
guard.swap-used: der belegte Swap liegt über seiner Linie und der verfügbare Speicher unter der Wiederaufnahmelinie
guard.swap-share: der Anteil des belegten Swaps liegt über seiner Linie und der verfügbare Speicher unter der Wiederaufnahmelinie
guard.compressed: der komprimierte Speicher liegt über seiner Linie
guard.cap: ein baukritischer Prozess hat seine Speicherobergrenze überschritten
guard.swap-free: der noch freie Swap liegt unter einer Swap-Datei, ein Schub von Auslagerungen kann die nächste Swap-Datei überholen
guard.grant: ein Prozess liegt weit über dem Speicher, den seine Zusage reserviert hat, während der Host keinen freien Speicher mehr hat

danger.available: der verfügbare Speicher liegt unter der Gefahrenlinie
danger.headroom: der verfügbare Speicher plus noch wachsender Swap liegt unter der Gefahrenlinie der Reserve
danger.swap-used: der belegte Swap liegt über seiner Gefahrenlinie und der verfügbare Speicher unter der Wachlinie
danger.swap-share: der Anteil des belegten Swaps liegt über seiner Gefahrenlinie und der verfügbare Speicher unter der Wachlinie
danger.compressed: der komprimierte Speicher liegt über seiner Gefahrenlinie
danger.swap-free: der noch freie Swap liegt unter einer halben Swap-Datei, der Kernel kann ohne Swap dastehen, bevor die nächste Datei existiert
danger.swapping: der Host lagert Speicher mit hoher Rate aus, obwohl der Speicherdruck noch nicht kritisch ist

reasons.limit: es blieb über das harte Maximum hinaus angehalten, ohne dass sich der Host erholte; es wird abgebrochen, damit sein Client es erneut versuchen kann
reasons.cap: sein Speicher liegt über der Obergrenze von {cap} MB für {kind}
reasons.capCrossed: sein Speicher hat die Obergrenze von {cap} MB für {kind} überschritten; die Art ist baukritisch, daher wird zuerst anderes angehalten und erst bei kritischem Host abgebrochen
reasons.ceiling: Einheit {unit} erreichte {peak} MB und liegt über ihrer Obergrenze {ceilingKind} von {ceiling} MB; sie steht nicht auf der Carving-Liste: entlang der Domänen-Taxonomie schneiden, damit sie passt
reasons.ceilingListed: Einheit {unit} erreichte {peak} MB und liegt über ihrem erklärten Carving-Budget von {ceiling} MB (gemessen {measured} MB): weiter schneiden oder neu messen und das neue Budget eintragen
reasons.guard: der Host hatte knappen Speicher (angespannt) und der Prozess blieb zu lange angehalten
reasons.danger: der Host hatte kritisch wenig Speicher

grant.within: ; er hielt {megabytes} MB, innerhalb seiner Zusage von {grant} MB, und wurde nur genommen, weil der Host in Gefahr war
grant.over: ; er hielt {megabytes} MB, {excess} MB über seiner Zusage von {grant} MB

failure.head: [Wächter] der Build kann nicht enden: der Host-Wächter hat {count} seiner Prozesse abgebrochen, damit dieser Rechner nicht ohne Speicher gerät
failure.tail: Es wird nichts wiederholt. Die oben genannte Ursache beheben (eine Einheit über ihrer Obergrenze schneiden) oder warten, bis der Host-Speicher ruhig ist, dann den Befehl erneut ausführen.
failure.exhausted: Der Build wurde {retries} Mal erneut eingereiht, und der Host-Speicher blieb nicht ruhig. Warten, bis der Host-Speicher ruhig ist, dann den Befehl erneut ausführen.

requeue.wait: [Wächter] der Host-Wächter hat {count} der Prozesse dieses Builds abgebrochen, damit der Host nicht ohne Speicher gerät ({kinds}); der Build wird erneut zur Kapazitätszulassung eingereiht, sobald der Host-Speicher ruhig ist (Versuch {attempt} von {maximum})
requeue.waiting: [Wächter] Warten auf ruhigen Host-Speicher, {seconds} s von {limit} s, bevor der Build erneut zugelassen wird
requeue.admit: [Wächter] der Build wird erneut zugelassen (Versuch {attempt} von {maximum})

de.held: [Wächter] {operation} wartet: der Hostspeicher ist {level} ({trigger}); nichts Schweres startet, bis er wieder ruhig ist (verfügbar {available} MB, Swap belegt {swap} MB, komprimiert {compressed} MB)
de.status: Speicherwächter: {level} ({mode}), {trigger}; verfügbar {available} von {total} MB, Swap belegt {swap} MB, komprimiert {compressed} MB, Druck {pressure}; angehalten {suspended}, fortgesetzt {resumed}, abgebrochen {cancelled}
de.statusAbsent: Speicherwächter: auf diesem Rechner läuft kein Wächter
de.locked: [Wächter] ein anderer Wächter hält die Sperre (pid {pid}); dieser endet
de.left: [Wächter] {kind} pid {pid} fortgesetzt, von einem Vorgänger angehalten zurückgelassen
de.observeOnly: [Wächter] Plattform {platform} kann Prozesse nicht anhalten: nur Beobachtungsmodus

reasonsStopped.code: der eigene Quelltext hat sich geändert
